$comment: Shared source of truth for SPA URLs that must survive a HARD load (typed, pasted, bookmarked, or arrived at from an email link) -- i.e. the browser asks the server for them before any JS runs. Two tests read this file and they must BOTH pass: src/router.test.tsx proves each sample matches a React route (and that no top-level React route lacks a sample), and test/engram_web/spa_route_parity_test.exs proves each sample resolves in the Phoenix router. Neither list can drift without the other going red. This exists because /reset-password had a React route and no Phoenix route: it survived only by falling through a root wildcard, and deleting that wildcard silently broke self-host password recovery with every test green. `devOnly` lists routes that exist ONLY under import.meta.env.DEV and are served by the Vite dev server, never by Phoenix; they are exempt from parity on purpose, not by omission. `mustNotResolve` is the other half: URL shapes that were RETIRED (the pre-/v root vault routes) or that must not become soft-404s (over-deep vault paths returning a 200 shell). A manifest of routes that exist cannot catch a route that was deleted, or a wildcard that got too greedy -- this list can.
